open_points.subject: M07 PublicationMark marked_at
open_points.question: What source supplies `marked_at`, what datetime representation and precision are stored, and how many clock readings does one mark operation take?
options: Read an aware UTC system clock once and store that instant in a specified UTC representation.
Read local time or a naive UTC clock, with implementation-chosen precision.
Allow the persistence backend or database to generate the timestamp.
open_points.default_guess: Inject a clock, read it exactly once when creating the first mark, and store a naive UTC datetime at the model's specified precision.

witness.initial: A placement exists and has no publication mark.
events: The calling flow asks the deliverer to record a Portal photo id.
The deliverer creates M07 and writes `marked_at`.
outcomes: One implementation reads an injected UTC clock once and stores naive UTC.
Another lets the database generate local time or reads the clock more than once and stores a different representation or instant.
witness.observer: The calling flow or an operator reading the persisted mark sees a different `marked_at` value or representation.

open_points.subject: A8 ServiceExit listening boundary
open_points.text:
The service has begun listening once its web server reports
its startup complete, its socket accepting connections; that report is the boundary.
open_points.question: Which concrete event is authoritative when the server's startup-complete report and the socket becoming able to accept connections are not observably simultaneous?
options: The web server's startup-complete report is the boundary, regardless of a later observable accept.
The successful bind/listen or actual ability to accept connections is the boundary.
Startup is complete only after both conditions have been independently established.
open_points.default_guess: Use the web server's documented startup-complete event, but only if its contract guarantees that the socket is already listening.

witness.initial: The process is starting and has not yet been classified as having served.
events: The web server emits its startup-complete report.
Before the socket can accept a connection, SIGTERM stops the process cleanly.
outcomes: Treating the report as the boundary gives SERVED and exit status 0.
Treating socket acceptance as the boundary gives START_FAILED and exit status 1.
witness.observer: The process supervisor sees a different exit status.

open_points.subject: A8 ServiceExit boundary equality
open_points.text:
START_FAILED, value `start_failed`: the process ends before that boundary, whatever ends it, a signal
included; SERVED, value `served`: after it, a SIGINT or SIGTERM stops the web server, which returns without
an error, and nothing fails until the process ends; and SERVER_FAILED, value `server_failed`: after it, the
process ends in any other way
open_points.question: How is an end, signal, or failure occurring at the boundary itself classified, since the rules cover only before and after it?
options: Treat the boundary event as already served, so events at it use the after-boundary rules.
Treat events in the same transition as before the boundary completed.
Define an explicit ordering within the startup-complete transition.
open_points.default_guess: Make successful completion of the startup callback happen first; subsequent events, even in the same event-loop turn, use the after-boundary rules.

open_points.subject: A8 ServiceExit failure
open_points.text:
nothing fails until the process ends; and SERVER_FAILED, value `server_failed`: after it, the
process ends in any other way, a failure during or after the shutdown of a stopped server included, so any
failure after the boundary outranks the signal.
open_points.question: What exactly counts as a failure after the boundary, including cleanup, logging, telemetry, signal-handler, task-cancellation, and process-exit errors?
options: Any exception or nonzero result in any process shutdown activity is a failure.
Only failure of the web server or application lifecycle is a failure; ancillary cleanup failures do not change SERVED.
List the components and error classes whose failures change the outcome.
open_points.default_guess: Treat every uncaught exception or nonzero lifecycle/shutdown result before process termination as a failure, while ignoring explicitly handled best-effort ancillary errors.

witness.initial: The service has crossed the boundary and is accepting connections.
events: The web server returns without error.
A best-effort telemetry or log flush raises an exception during final cleanup.
outcomes: Counting all shutdown exceptions gives SERVER_FAILED and exit status 1.
Treating ancillary cleanup as outside the service failure condition gives SERVED and exit status 0.
witness.observer: The process supervisor sees a different exit status.

open_points.subject: context: ServiceExit members
open_points.text:
Its members are exactly `start_failed`, `served` and `server_failed`; A8
decides what each means and its status.
open_points.rule:
Член, названный одним значением, — нарушение: значение с точкой или дефисом не
является именем ни одного члена, генератор пишет только имена
(`AuditAction.EXPENSE_CREATE`), и валидатор отклоняет такую note
(`note_enum_member_by_value`).
open_points.question: Name each member by its generated member name beside `= models.ServiceExit`, with the lowercase value only as an optional supplement.
